title: Aromatic Claisen rearrangement
subtitle: Allyl phenyl ether becomes 2-allylphenol: a [3,3] shift, then the ring is made aromatic again

ether.caption: allyl phenyl ether in N,N-diethylaniline (the solvent)
ether.learnerPrompt: The allyl group moves from oxygen to the ring by a [3,3] shift. Draw that step first.
hintTiers: Find the 1,5-diene pattern: allyl C=C, CH₂, oxygen, then a C=C of the ring. Six atoms, six electrons. Which ring carbon is at the end of the six?
The ortho ring carbon bonds to the far CH₂ of the allyl group, the O–CH₂ bond breaks, and oxygen gains a C=O. The aromatic ring is broken for now. Three arrows.

Arrow 1: from the ring C=C π bond (between the oxygen-bearing carbon and the ortho carbon) to a new bond between the ortho carbon and the far CH₂ of the allyl group. Arrow 2: from the O–allyl σ bond to the bond between oxygen and its ring carbon (it becomes C=O). Arrow 3: from the allyl C=C π bond to the bond between its CH and the CH₂ that lost oxygen.

misconceptions.feedbackMessage: Breaking the O–allyl bond on its own would give a phenoxide and an allyl cation. Here the bond breaks only as the new C–C bond forms, in one cyclic step.

The carbon carrying oxygen is only four atoms round from the allyl end. Count six: oxygen, its ring carbon, the next (ortho) ring carbon, and the three allyl carbons. The new bond is to the ortho carbon.
The amine is only the solvent for now: there is no acidic proton yet. First the allyl group moves to the ring.

partialProgressMessages.feedbackMessage: Right: the ortho carbon bonds to the allyl end. Now the oxygen side: the O–allyl bond gives its pair to make C=O, and the allyl π bond moves across. Two more arrows.

dienone.caption: 6-allylcyclohexa-2,4-dien-1-one, not aromatic
dienone.learnerPrompt: The ring has lost its aromaticity. A base can win it back: remove the right proton.
hintTiers: The ring carbon that took the allyl group now has an H as well. Which proton, if removed, lets the ring become aromatic again?
The amine nitrogen takes the H from the ring carbon carrying the allyl group; that C–H pair makes a ring C=C and the C=O pair goes onto oxygen. Three arrows: a phenoxide forms.

Arrow 1: amine nitrogen lone pair to a new bond to the H on the allyl-bearing ring carbon. Arrow 2: from that C–H bond to the bond between this carbon and the carbonyl carbon. Arrow 3: from the C=O π bond to a lone pair on oxygen.

misconceptions.feedbackMessage: That runs the [3,3] shift backwards. The dienone is far less stable than an aromatic phenol, so it is drained away by losing a proton.
A tertiary amine adding to the C=O leads nowhere. Use the amine as a base to remove the proton on the allyl-bearing ring carbon.

partialProgressMessages.feedbackMessage: Two of three. The carbonyl carbon would now have five bonds: its C=O π pair moves onto oxygen.

phenoxide.caption: 2-allylphenoxide + N,N-diethylanilinium ion
phenoxide.learnerPrompt: Finish: put the proton back where it belongs.
hintTiers: The ring is aromatic again. The negative charge is on oxygen, and the anilinium ion holds a proton.
Oxygen takes the proton from the anilinium ion. Two arrows.
Arrow 1: oxygen lone pair to a new bond to the N–H proton. Arrow 2: from the N–H bond to a lone pair on nitrogen.

misconceptions.feedbackMessage: That puts the proton back on the ring carbon and remakes the non-aromatic dienone. Protonate oxygen: the ring stays aromatic.

partialProgressMessages.feedbackMessage: Right: oxygen takes the proton. The N–H bond's pair goes back to nitrogen. One more arrow.

steps.explanationAfterStep: A Claisen rearrangement with one of the ring's C=C bonds as the vinyl part. The allyl group is turned round: its far CH₂ end is now on the ortho carbon. The price is the ring's aromaticity, which is why such a high temperature is needed.
Losing the proton at the ring carbon that took the allyl group turns the dienone into an aromatic phenoxide: the regained aromaticity drives this tautomerisation completely.

Proton transfer to oxygen gives 2-allylphenol and returns the amine. Overall the dienone has tautomerised to the phenol, as a ketone goes to its enol, except that here the enol (the phenol) is the far more stable form.

mechanismSummary: Heating allyl phenyl ether makes the allyl group move from oxygen to the ortho carbon by a [3,3]-sigmatropic (Claisen) shift; the allyl group is inverted on the way, so its far end becomes attached. The dienone formed is a non-aromatic keto tautomer; losing and regaining a proton (here with the amine solvent as base) gives the aromatic 2-allylphenol. If both ortho positions are blocked, the dienone undergoes a second [3,3] shift (a Cope) to put the allyl group at the para position.
references: Clayden, Greeves and Warren, Organic Chemistry, 2nd edition (Oxford University Press), chapter 35
